concept.title: DualArrayDeque 的按位更新
concept.core_question: DualArrayDeque 如何把按位插入删除转交给正确的内部栈？
concept.summary: 位置落在前半段时用反向下标操作 front，否则用偏移后的下标操作 back，随后检查平衡。
concept.definition: DualArrayDeque 根据 i 是否小于 front.size() 选择内部栈。前半段使用反向下标，后半段使用减去 front.size() 的局部下标；add 与 remove 完成后调用 balance。忽略平衡成本，更新时间为 $O(1+\min\{i,n-i\})$。

relations.description: 理解《DualArrayDeque 的按位更新》是继续学习目标知识点的直接基础。

rookie_explanation.analogy: 管理员先判断目标卡片属于左摞还是右摞，再换算成该摞内部的位置完成操作，最后检查两摞是否过度失衡。
rookie_explanation.boundary: 类比不展开 balance 搬移元素的具体步骤和摊还成本。

related_concepts.title: DualArrayDeque 的双栈表示
related_concepts.core_question: DualArrayDeque 如何用两个 ArrayStack 表示一个逻辑序列？
related_concepts.summary: front 逆序保存前半段，back 正序保存后半段，元素总数等于两个栈的 size 之和。
related_concepts.definition: DualArrayDeque 用 front 与 back 两个 ArrayStack 表示 List。front 逆序保存逻辑前缀，back 正序保存逻辑后缀，$n=front.size()+back.size()$。若 $i<front.size()$，对应 front 中的下标为 $front.size()-i-1$；否则对应 back 中的 $i-front.size()$。

related_concepts.title: ArrayStack 的按位插入
related_concepts.core_question: ArrayStack 在位置 i 插入元素时为什么要向右搬移元素？
related_concepts.summary: 插入前需确保容量足够，再把区间 i 到 n-1 右移一格，空出 a[i] 后写入新元素。
related_concepts.definition: ArrayStack 的 add(i,x) 在后备数组已满时先扩容，然后把原有下标 i 至 n-1 的元素按从右到左的安全顺序整体右移一位，把 x 写入 a[i]，最后令 n 增加 1。忽略扩容时，其时间为 $O(n-i)$。

related_concepts.title: ArrayStack 的按位删除
related_concepts.core_question: ArrayStack 删除位置 i 的元素时为什么要向左搬移元素？
related_concepts.summary: 删除 a[i] 后需把 i+1 到 n-1 的元素左移填补空位，因此忽略缩容时耗时 O(n-i)。
related_concepts.definition: ArrayStack 的 remove(i) 先保存 a[i]，再把下标 i+1 至 n-1 的元素整体左移一位覆盖空缺，令 n 减少 1，并在数组空闲比例达到阈值时触发 resize，最后返回被删除值。忽略 resize 时，其时间为 $O(n-i)$。

related_concepts.title: DualArrayDeque 的再平衡
related_concepts.core_question: DualArrayDeque 在什么条件下重新分配 front 与 back 的元素？
related_concepts.summary: 当一侧超过另一侧三倍时，balance 按逻辑顺序重建两栈，使两侧分别约占一半。
related_concepts.definition: 当元素数至少为 2 且 front 与 back 的大小相差超过 3 倍时，DualArrayDeque 的 balance 按逻辑序列重建两个 ArrayStack，使 front 保存前 $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ 个元素并逆序排列，back 保存其余 $\lceil n/2\rceil$ 个元素并正序排列。一次重建移动 $O(n)$ 个元素。

source_records.content: Note that if an index $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}<\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}}$, then it corresponds to the element of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} at position $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}-1$, since the elements of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} are stored in reverse order. Adding and removing elements from a DualArrayDeque is illustrated in \figref{dualarraydeque}. The \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operation manipulates either \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} or \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}}}, as appropriate:

A sequence of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operations on a DualArrayDeque. Arrows denote elements being copied. Operations that result in a rebalancing by \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} are marked with an asterisk.

The \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} method performs rebalancing of the two ArrayStacks \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}}}, by calling the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} method. The implementation of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is described below, but for now it is sufficient to know that \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} ensures that, unless $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{size}()}}<2$, \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} do not differ by more than a factor of 3. In particular, $3\cdot\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \ge \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}}$ and $3\cdot\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \ge \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}}$. Next we analyze the cost of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}}, ignoring the cost of calls to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}}. If $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}<\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}}$, then \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} gets implemented by the call to $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()-\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}-1,x})}$. The second case \myeqref{das-back} occurs when $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}\ge 3\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/4$. When $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/4\le\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}<3\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/4$, we cannot be sure whether the operation affects \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} or \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}}}, but in either case, the operation takes $O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}})=O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}})=O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}})$ time, since $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}\ge \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/4$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}-\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{i}}}}> \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/4$. The \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operation and its analysis resemble the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} operation and analysis.
